We are looking for an exceptional Senior Director to be the single face of this program from Telesat to DND – owning the customer relationship and orchestrating delivery from build through to operational service. If you are energized by high-stakes defence programs, thrive at the intersection of customer, commercial and engineering, and want to help shape a nation’s strategic communications capability, this is a rare and career-defining role. This is as much a technical and program-delivery leadership role as it is a customer role: you will bring genuine engineering fluency and deep program management discipline to steer a complex, multi-segment space and ground system from build through to in-service operation.

Role Summary: The Senior Director oversees the development, initial deployment, and ongoing engagement over the entire life of the ESCP-P program (LEO Mil-Ka and MEO UHF/X-band). You will be the primary relationship owner and “one face” of the program to DND – accountable for customer trust, implementation progress, program health, and the seamless coordination of every Telesat function that touches the mission. In the initial program phase, to succeed, you must pair strong technical background with deep, hands-on program management experience: you will engage credibly with engineering and systems teams on architecture, conops, design, integration, test and acceptance, while engaging with the Program Delivery team to hold the program to rigorous schedule, cost, risk and quality discipline.
 This is a matrixed leadership role: while you own the customer-facing program, you will work laterally across sales, engineering, product, network operations, security, supply chain, legal, finance and program management teams and Telesat’s strategic partner MDA Space to keep commitments on track. Success depends on influence, orchestration and executive presence as much as direct authority. It also demands real technical depth and program management rigor: you will be trusted to translate between the customer’s mission needs and Telesat’s engineering and delivery teams, interrogate technical trade-offs, and keep a large, multi-year build predictable and auditable.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Own the customer relationship – serve as the single, trusted point of contact and “one face” of Telesat to DND, building durable, credible relationships across the customer’s program, technical and executive stakeholders.
 Lead end-to-end program engagement – oversee the development, initial deployment, and ongoing service engagement across the full ESCP-P lifecycle from initial service access to full operational capability , spanning LEO Mil-Ka and MEO UHF/X-band capabilities.
 Orchestrate across a matrixed organization – coordinating with Program Delivery, align and drive contributions from engineering, network operations, product, security, supply chain, legal, finance and Go To Market.
 Govern program health – in conjunction with Program Delivery, manage scope, schedule, cost, risk and quality against contractual commitments; establish the cadence, governance and reporting that keep the program predictable and on track.
 Co-ordinate technical program leadership – bring an engineering-literate perspective to engage the technical teams with customer expectations regarding system design, integration, verification and acceptance across the LEO Mil-Ka and MEO UHF/X-band portions of the program, working with Program Delivery to ensure technical trade-offs, dependencies and risks are well understood and soundly managed.
 Apply deep program management rigor – working with Program Delivery, deploy proven program management methods (integrated master schedule, earned-value/cost control, risk and dependency management, and formal milestone/gate reviews) to keep a complex, multi-year build disciplined, transparent and auditable.
 Translate mission needs into delivery – ensure customer requirements, timelines and mission priorities are clearly understood internally and reflected in system and product specifications and operational roadmaps and procedures.
 Lead the joint governance – represent Telesat in the DND / Telesat Joint program management office and associated working groups, driving decisions, resolving issues and escalating effectively.
 Protect commercial and contractual outcomes – partner with commercial, legal and finance teams to safeguard revenue, manage change, and ensure obligations are met with full compliance and transparency.
 Champion assurance and security – working with Program Delivery and engineering teams, uphold the security, sovereignty and mission-assurance standards expected of a defence program of national importance.
Ideal Candidate Requirements: You are a seasoned program and customer leader who has carried the trust of major clients on complex, high-value programs. You combine that a solid technical background and deep, demonstrable program management experience on large, technically demanding programs. Specifically, you bring:
 Large customer / account leadership background – a proven track record managing major, complex customer relationships and large-scale programs, ideally as the senior accountable interface to the client.
 Large technical program experience - a solid grounding in complex engineering programs (ideally satellite, space, telecommunications, networks or systems integration), with the ability to engage credibly with engineering teams on architecture, integration, test and acceptance, and to challenge, interpret and communicate technical detail. Extensive, hands-on experience directing large, multi-year technical programs, with mastery of integrated scheduling, earned-value/cost control, risk and dependency management, and formal milestone/gate governance; recognized program management credentials (e.g., PMP or equivalent) are a strong asset
 Canadian defence experience – direct experience working with the Canadian defence community (DND / CAF and related agencies), with a strong understanding of how defence programs are governed, delivered and assured.
 Government of Canada Secret Security clearance – you currently hold, or are eligible to obtain, a Secret-level security clearance.
 Ottawa-based – located in (or willing to relocate to) the Ottawa, Ontario area to enable close, on-site engagement with the customer and Telesat leadership.
 Matrixed leadership ability – demonstrated success leading and delivering through influence in a highly matrixed organization, aligning diverse technical and commercial teams toward shared outcomes.
 Executive presence & communication – exceptional stakeholder management, negotiation and communication skills, comfortable operating from the boardroom to the technical working group.
 Program discipline – strong command of program governance, risk, schedule and financial management on large, multi-year engagements. You are comfortable with an integrated master schedule and earned-value reporting, and leading technically complex delivery to plan.
 Preferred – background in satellite, telecommunications or a related technology domain, and familiarity with defence procurement, ITB and program delivery frameworks.
Why Join Us: Take the lead on one of Canada’s most strategically significant defence communications programs with visible national impact.
 Own the customer relationship end-to-end and shape how a next-generation LEO network is delivered into service.
 Work at the forefront of Telesat Lightspeed, a global-first LEO constellation, alongside world-class engineering and commercial teams.
 Apply and deepen your technical expertise and program management craft at the leading edge of space systems engineering and large-scale defence program delivery.
 A senior director-level platform with executive visibility, meaningful autonomy, and the opportunity to build and grow a program franchise.

 About the role: 
The AVP, Security Architecture is a senior leader accountable for the enterprise security architecture strategy, governance, and evolution of security capabilities across global business and technology environments. 
The role translates business priorities, cyber risk appetite, and emerging threats into architecture direction that protects clients, employees, information, and critical services.
Working closely with the CISO, CTO, enterprise architects, and business technology leaders, the AVP leads the Security Architecture function and embeds secure-by-design, Zero Trust, and defense-in-depth principles into enterprise transformation and solution delivery.
The AVP serves as a senior security design authority within enterprise architecture governance, shapes security investment priorities, and develops a team that provides consistent architectural guidance across business units and geographies.
 What You Will Do?
Key Responsibilities:
 1. Enterprise Security Architecture Strategy and Road mapping 
 Own the enterprise security architecture strategy and target state across identity, cloud, infrastructure, networks, endpoints, applications, data, and security platforms.
 Establish multi-year security capability roadmaps aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture, the cybersecurity strategy, and organizational risk appetite.
 Translate capability assessments, threat trends, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework into prioritized architecture improvements, with Zero Trust and defense in depth guiding modernization.
 2. Security Architecture Function and People Leadership 
 Lead and develop the Security Architecture team, with accountability for performance, coaching, succession planning, and the skills required to support enterprise priorities.
 Define the function's operating model, engagement processes, and service expectations, providing architecture coverage across security programs and business-led technology initiatives.
 Prioritize demand and allocate capacity across strategic planning, project assurance, governance, and emerging technology work; establish coverage and knowledge-sharing practices that reduce dependence on individual specialists.
 Manage the function's operating plan, assigned budget, and resources, and build business cases for additional capacity or specialist support.
 3. Architecture Governance and Design Authority 
 Establish security reference architectures, standards, reusable patterns, and guardrails in partnership with global domain architects and enterprise security policy owners.
 Serve as senior security design authority for significant initiatives within the enterprise architecture governance process, with clear decision rights and escalation paths.
 Represent Security Architecture on enterprise technology review boards, resolve cross-domain design issues, and oversee design assurance against approved security requirements.
 Oversee recommendations for architectural exceptions, compensating controls, and remediation plans; escalate material residual risks to accountable business and risk owners through established governance.
 4. Secure Solution Design and Transformation Oversight 
 Provide security architecture oversight for major business and technology initiatives from early planning through implementation, with review effort proportionate to risk and complexity.
 Embed threat modelling, secure design reviews, and reusable security patterns into delivery practices, partnering with application, data, infrastructure, cloud, and engineering teams.
 Lead architectural direction for security transformation programs, including identity modernization, cloud security, network segmentation, application security, data protection, and cyber recovery.
 5. Security Capability Portfolio and Investment Leadership 
 Direct the strategic evolution, integration, consolidation, and retirement of security tools, services, and capabilities to address enterprise needs and reduce fragmentation.
 Shape investment priorities and present business cases that assess risk reduction, control coverage, technical feasibility, interoperability, operational capacity, and total cost of ownership.
 Maintain an enterprise view of capability gaps, overlapping technologies, lifecycle risks, and technical debt; partner with engineering, operations, procurement, and vendor management to turn roadmaps into achievable investment and delivery plans.
 6. Technology Evaluation and AI Security 
 Evaluate emerging security technologies, vendor capabilities, and service models, providing recommendations on suitability, integration, scalability, and long-term viability.
 Sponsor proofs of concept with clear success criteria for security effectiveness, technical compatibility, operational readiness, and business value.
 Define security architecture requirements and patterns for AI platforms, generative AI, and autonomous agents, addressing identity, data access, tool permissions, monitoring, and human oversight.
 Identify opportunities to use automation and AI within security capabilities, working with responsible teams to validate benefits, control effectiveness, and operational accountability.
 7. Architectural Risk and Resilience 
 Identify systemic security architecture weaknesses and drive mitigation roadmaps with accountable engineering, platform, and business technology owners.
 Translate security, privacy, regulatory, and data residency requirements into architecture requirements in partnership with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, and Legal.
 Integrate requirements for resilience, ransomware containment, recovery, logging, and monitoring into security designs, working with operational owners to establish implementation and validation expectations.
 Use findings from incidents, security testing, audits, and control assessments to improve reference architectures, patterns, and capability roadmaps.
 8. Executive Engagement and Enterprise Partnership 
 Act as a trusted advisor to the Global Chief Enterprise Architect, CISO, CTO, CIO, and business technology leaders on security architecture strategy and significant technology decisions.
 Translate complex architecture choices into clear business implications, investment options, delivery dependencies, and risk treatment recommendations for executive forums.
 Build alignment across global business units and technology functions, resolve competing priorities, and report on architecture coverage, adoption, roadmap progress, and outcomes.
 What Do You Need to Succeed? 
 Qualifications Required: 
 University degree or college diploma in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
 15+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity architecture, engineering, or related technology leadership roles, including accountability for enterprise security architecture strategy.
 Demonstrated experience leading and developing architecture or security teams, managing priorities and resources, and delivering outcomes in a complex, matrixed organization.
 Experience influencing VP and SVP stakeholders and presenting architecture strategies, investment recommendations, and risk decisions at executive forums.
 Strong knowledge across identity and access management, cloud, infrastructure, network, endpoint, application, API, and data security, including cryptography and secrets management.
 Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise architecture standards, reference patterns, governance processes, and multi-year security capability roadmaps.
 Practical understanding of Zero Trust, defense in depth, threat modelling, secure development, and frameworks such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
 Experience modernizing security platforms and evaluating vendors or third-party services for technical feasibility, integration, control effectiveness, and total cost of ownership.
 Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with the judgment to balance security, business value, delivery constraints, and operational sustainability.
 Preferred skills: 
 Experience in financial services or another regulated industry with global operations and complex privacy or data residency requirements.
 Experience with hybrid and multi-cloud environments, including AWS, Azure, or Alibaba Cloud.
 Experience defining security architectures for AI, autonomous agents, automation, or other emerging technologies.
 Experience with major security transformations, technology rationalization, or mergers and acquisitions integration.
 Relevant professional certifications, such as CISSP, CISM, SABSA, TOGAF, or cloud security and architecture certifications.
 Key Outcomes and Measures of Success:

 Architecture coverage: Timely engagement on significant initiatives across business units, with consistent service coverage and review turnaround.
 Secure delivery: Greater use of approved patterns and earlier resolution of design weaknesses, reducing avoidable rework and exceptions.
 Risk treatment: Progress against remediation plans for material architectural weaknesses and timely escalation of unresolved risks.
 Portfolio effectiveness: Reduced capability duplication and technical debt, supported by documented control improvements and lifecycle cost benefits.

ABOUT GEORGIAN



Georgian is a Toronto-based venture capital firm that partners with high-growth technology companies across cybersecurity, AI software, robotics, defense. We manage about $6B in assets and we have invested in more than 80 companies that we support with capital and technical capability.



Our in-house AI lab works directly with portfolio companies to provide a differentiated experience across the investment lifecycle, and drives the adoption of AI for our internal operations.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE



Are you an aspiring AI Engineer eager to gain real-world impact and learn how to push AI's boundaries? Imagine diving into diverse, cutting-edge AI problems across multiple high-growth companies with the support of a leading VC firm. That's Georgian.



We're not your typical VC. Georgian's unique R&D team partners directly with our portfolio companies, providing the technical horsepower and strategic guidance to help accelerate their AI initiatives. We also play a critical role in our investment process, conducting deep technical diligence to identify promising AI-driven businesses.



Think of it as working in a dynamic startup environment, but without the inherent risks of a single venture. You'll tackle fascinating challenges, meet and potentially work with brilliant founders and CTOs, and try to help unearth the next generation of industry leaders. It's a fun, engaging, and highly impactful way to build your career.




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS



Georgian's mission is to empower the world's leading B2B software companies with an unfair advantage, accelerating their participation in the digital economy. As an AI Engineer Intern on our R&D team, you'll support this mission by contributing to cutting-edge machine learning projects. You'll assist in bringing machine learning expertise directly to our portfolio companies' most pressing challenges, helping them build and scale potentially transformative AI products. You'll also contribute to our investment process technical diligence, helping us identify innovative and technically sound companies.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DELIVER



 - Support AI system development. Assist in building LLM agents, Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines and fine‑tuned domain‑specific models under guidance; help implement workflows with frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex/PydanticAI.

 - Contribute to portfolio projects. Support Georgian "strike teams" embedded in portfolio companies; assist with code implementation, testing, and documentation.

 - Technical analysis & documentation. Help convert technical concepts into clear documentation; support preparation of demos and presentations for stakeholders.

 - Hands‑on R&D support. Assist in rapid prototyping, run experiments and ablation studies, contribute to internal tech notes and documentation.

 - Support AI roadmap development. Help gather requirements in discovery workshops, assist in documenting technical specifications and implementation plans.

 - Contribute to safety & governance. Assist in implementing evaluation pipelines and testing frameworks to keep models reliable and compliant.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR




IDEAL ATTRIBUTES

 - Education & Experience: Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Statistics, or a related quantitative discipline with a focus on machine learning, optimization theory, or related areas.

 - Hands-On Foundation: Familiarity with deep learning toolkits such as Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch. Understanding of GenAI, LLM tooling and Context Engineering fundamentals.

 - Software Development: Proficiency in Python and foundational software development skills, enabling you to write clean, efficient code.

 - Problem Formulation & Communication: The ability to understand applied research problems, assist in designing experiments, implement solutions, and clearly document findings for diverse audiences with varying technical backgrounds.

 - Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to work on team projects, collaborate effectively with technical groups, and communicate progress to mentors and stakeholders.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience contributing to open-source AI/ML-related projects or research papers.

 - Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) for MLOps and model deployment.

 - Exposure to specific industry verticals relevant to Georgian's portfolio (e.g., vertical SaaS, cybersecurity, healthcare tech, fintech).




CULTURAL ATTRIBUTES WE LOVE



 - High ambition & agency: You're allergic to incrementalism and thrive in low‑structure, high‑ownership settings.

 - Insatiable curiosity: You debug the root cause and ask why until everyone else gets annoyed—in a good way.

 - Team over ego: You amplify colleagues and founders alike, seeing leverage in elevating the collective.

 - Commercial storytelling: You speak with brevity and distill complexity so a time‑starved CEO instantly sees value.




HIRING PROCESS



We don't hire like a MAG7 or scale up — in fact we rarely hire compared to them.



You shouldn't expect a cookie-cutter high-volume hiring process with us — but a more boutique one that allows you to see a lot of the organization before joining us.



We build a thesis in what an individual brings to our very small team, versus simply matching qualifications:

 1. 30‑min intro (values & motivations)

 2. 60‑min technical interview (ML fundamentals & problem‑solving)

 3. Project discussion with team members




POSITION STATUS

 

This posting represents an active, future internship vacancy on our team. We will be interviewing for this role in early 2027.

 


OUR COMMITMENT TO ACCESSIBILITY



Georgian is dedicated to building an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We provide reasonable accommodations throughout our recruitment process to ensure every candidate has the opportunity to perform at their best. If you require any specific accommodations at any stage, please reach out to us at peopleteam [at]  georgian.io.




USE OF AI



Innovation is at our core and we use artificial intelligence (AI) to support parts of our hiring process, such as screening and evaluating applications. These tools are designed to assist - not replace - human decision making and all final hiring decisions are made by our team.  We regularly review our AI tools to help promote fairness and reduce the risk of unintended bias. If you have any questions about how we use AI in our process or would like more information, please contact us at careers [at] georgian.io.

PSTs are vital to the filmmaking process and essential to maintaining the integrity and efficiency of the pipeline.
 PSTs are not just responsible for managing tasks like cue management, backups, and data transfer, but also building, maintaining, and optimizing the tools and pipelines that drive these processes. By developing and modifying python tools and scripts throughout the course of a show, PSTs ensure that these tasks become seamless and efficient, even during high-pressure crunch times. The true value of a PST lies in their ability to automate and streamline workflows, making complex tasks effortless, preventing bottlenecks, and ensuring that production remains uninterrupted and efficient, no matter the scale.
 With deep expertise in the facility's departments, pipeline, and workflows, PSTs gain invaluable exposure across production, positioning them as strong candidates for career advancement and diverse opportunities within the company. Many former PSTs have advanced into prominent positions, including production management, technical direction, software development, systems engineering, and artist roles. This position provides a unique opportunity to build a broad skill set, paving the way for long-term career growth. For more information about the PST program, please watch our recruiting video .

 Pipeline Optimization and Tool Development: Leverage software engineering to optimize critical tools and pipelines for tasks such as render farm management, media manipulation, reviews, client/vendor ingest, and deliveries, automating processes to ensure seamless workflows, eliminate bottlenecks, and maintain production efficiency, even during high-pressure crunch times.

Following established guidelines based on both internal and show-specific standards to maintain accurate data locations, file types, naming standards, resolution/colorspace specifications, audio/video codecs, and security allowances.
 Ingest/Deliveries: Ingest and deliver high-priority media from vendors and clients, ensuring it conforms to facility standards, is transferred between locations following security & firewall policies all while automating processes to enhance efficiency and streamline workflows.
 Technical Support and Communication: Serve as a key liaison between production, digital artists, and support teams, providing technical expertise that ensures seamless integration and smooth workflows, while effectively communicating with both technical and non-technical team members.
 Issue Management: Submit prompt and detailed information through support channels, clearly communicating issues and potential solutions to Color Scientists, Resources, Production, Systems, and Software teams, while monitoring critical servers & networks to minimize workflow disruptions and ensure swift resolution.
 Documentation and Testing: Test and document workflows, tools, and processes across I/O pipelines, command-line utilities, queuing plugins, directory and file structure management, proprietary software, and script-driven automation to ensure seamless and efficient production operations.

 Strong experience with Linux or UNIX operating systems

Affirm's engineering team is building a large-scale, highly-available, and global infrastructure that is shared across multiple financial products. Ensuring that our infrastructure is accessible to all engineers is critical to the success of the business. We pride ourselves on our culture across engineering of engaging in thorough technical design review, operational excellence, and capable incident response and analysis.
 The Compute Platform team owns the EKS foundation that Affirm's products run on, from cluster provisioning and lifecycle through the safety standards that keep thousands of workloads reliable at scale. Affirm operates 90+ EKS clusters across environments and regions, and this team is responsible for making that fleet standardized, automated, observable, and self-healing, while establishing and enforcing the workload configuration standards that protect availability. Our mission is to provide a secure, reliable, and scalable Kubernetes platform that lets infrastructure and application teams deploy and operate with confidence and minimal operational friction.
 What you’ll do 
 As a member of the Compute Platform organization, you will collaborate with other teams - including Product, Infrastructure, Traffic, Cost & Capacity Engineering to:
 Architect and evolve Affirm's EKS platform, driving strategy across cluster lifecycle, node management, and shared cluster components
 Lead the technical direction for cluster provisioning, upgrades, and teardown through standardized IaC (Terraform, Spacelift) and self-service workflows
 Own the reliability of core shared components across the fleet (Karpenter, CoreDNS, VPC CNI, Kube Proxy, Metrics Server, etc) and the CI/CD pipeline that ships them consistently
 Define and enforce EKS workload safety standards covering resource configuration, workload isolation and blast radius, disruption tolerance (PDBs), Karpenter consolidation strategies, etc
 Build the enforcement and automation path that moves each standard from research and white-glove onboarding through broad adoption to policy-enforced defaults for new workloads
 Establish the observability, baseline audits, and reporting needed to identify hot spots and measure risk mitigation over time
 Partner with cluster-user teams (checkout, batch, ML, analytics, DevProd, etc) to understand workload needs and shape the platform accordingly
 Drive cost and capacity strategy across node scaling, bin packing, and EC2 instance selection
 Mentor engineers across the Compute Platform teams and set the bar for operational excellence
 Participate in the on-call rotation, triage and catalogue runtime K8s issues, and collaborate with SRE on production incidents
 What we look for 
 Deep EKS and Kubernetes internals expertise, including cluster upgrades, node lifecycle, scheduling, and autoscaling (Karpenter, Cluster Autoscaler)
 Demonstrated experience automating Kubernetes operations at fleet scale, from cluster provisioning, upgrades, and node lifecycle to self-healing remediation and policy-driven enforcement, replacing manual toil with auditable, self-service workflows
 Strong grasp of workload reliability patterns: resource tuning, probes, PDBs, topology and isolation constraints
 Experience designing and enforcing platform standards through policy (admission control, OPA/Gatekeeper or equivalent) and automated frameworks
 Infrastructure as Code fluency with Terraform and a GitOps or pipeline-driven delivery model (ArgoCD, kube-applier, or similar)
 Observability instincts: defining SLOs, building metrics, logs, and alerting coverage, and running data-driven baseline audits
 Cross-functional collaboration skills with platform, product, SRE, and capacity teams
 Demonstrated mentorship and technical leadership across teams
 Drive to track emerging Kubernetes community best practices and adapt them to Affirm's needs
 Qualifications

 6+ years hands-on operating production Kubernetes at scale, ideally EKS on AWS
 Strong cloud-native architecture experience on AWS (EC2, VPC, IAM, EKS)
 Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, Spacelift a plus) and GitOps-style deployment pipelines
 Expert-level proficiency in Go or Python and a proven track record building production-grade Kubernetes controllers, operators, and platform tooling that other engineering teams depend on

WHAT'S THE ROLE 
 Great software engineering isn’t just about writing better code. It’s about creating the standards, structure and accountability that allow teams to build better solutions consistently.
 Dexterra is a services company, not a software engineering company, and that’s what makes this opportunity different. Technology supports a diverse and evolving business, with development happening across teams, functions and initiatives. As Software Engineering Architect, you’ll bring those efforts together, establish stronger engineering practices and create the structure needed to deliver secure, scalable and maintainable solutions.
 Reporting to the Enterprise Architect, you’ll take ownership of how software engineering is practised across Dexterra. Working cross-functionally with dispersed development teams, technology partners and business stakeholders, you’ll strengthen delivery, modernize enterprise platforms and help advance our internal software engineering and AI capabilities.
 This is an opportunity for someone who sees what can be better and takes ownership of making it happen.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 
 Own and evolve our software engineering practice , establishing clear standards, processes and expectations that improve consistency, quality and accountability.
 Connect development efforts across the organization , working cross-functionally with dispersed teams, technology partners and business stakeholders to create alignment around how software is designed, developed and delivered.
 Bring structure without unnecessary bureaucracy , introducing practical engineering disciplines that improve security, scalability, maintainability and delivery.
 Lead engineering activities supporting the modernization of enterprise platforms, including PVC Connect, with a focus on microservices, API-first development, integrations and scalable architecture.
 Establish and continuously improve engineering practices for CI/CD, code quality, observability, release management and secure software development.
 Strengthen delivery through effective technical and code reviews, proof-of-concept initiatives, quality controls and release-readiness practices.
 Partner with cybersecurity, architecture and cross-functional technology teams to embed security, compliance and enterprise standards into the development lifecycle.
 Help advance internal AI and software engineering capabilities, including AI-powered solutions, copilots, automation and productivity tools.
 Translate business requirements into clear technical scope, architecture decisions and achievable delivery plans.
 Identify opportunities to improve processes, tools and ways of working, then turn those opportunities into practical change.
 Mentor engineers, share knowledge and help build a culture grounded in quality, accountability, curiosity and continuous learning.
 Provide clear visibility into technical decisions, dependencies, risks and progress for technology and business stakeholders.
WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 
 You’re an experienced software engineering leader who combines technical depth with an ownership mindset. You know how to bring structure to complex development environments, align dispersed teams around better practices and influence change across an organization.
 Just as importantly, you’re curious about how things can work better. You’re comfortable challenging existing approaches, solving problems and turning ideas into practical improvements.
 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years in team or technical leadership.
 A degree or diploma in computer science, engineering, information systems or a related field.
 Experience modernizing legacy applications using microservices and API-first architectures.
 Strong knowledge of cloud engineering, CI/CD, DevOps, cybersecurity and secure software development.
 Experience with enterprise integrations and AI/ML or LLM-based solutions.
 The ability to coordinate dispersed teams, influence technical direction and translate business needs into practical solutions.
 Strong communication, stakeholder management and problem-solving skills.
 Ownership and Accountability: You take responsibility for outcomes, create clarity and follow through.
 Process Improvement: You challenge inefficient or inconsistent ways of working and turn opportunities into practical change.

An overview of this role 
 As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write and in the open source components they depend on.
 Your work spans complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.
 These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.
 What you do 
 Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead
 Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review
 Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes detection rules mapped to CWE and the test fixtures that prove they work.
 Package those analyzers for every place GitLab runs them, including CI jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, with findings reported in GitLab's standard security report formats
 Design and ship the manifest, lockfile, and SBOM parsing that tells the static analysis engine what a project depends on, and extend it to new ecosystems and formats
 Ship features across the automated remediation service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, from sandboxed updates to merge request creation
 Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, Engineering stakeholders such as Frontend and UX, and partner teams such as Code Scanning and Composition Analysis
